note: Freshness of every corpus here: when it was last checked against its official source, how, and whether global-law holds its newest commit. One row per corpus in data/freshness.tsv; `python tools/freshness.py <corpus or provision path>` reads them. A status is as of `as_of`; a corpus checked longer ago than its threshold has since become stale.

statuses.current: checked against the official source within its threshold, and global-law holds the newest commit
statuses.pending-change: the corpus has a newer commit than the one pinned here: a check held it, or the next pass will pin it
statuses.stale: not checked against the official source within its threshold
statuses.unverified: never checked against the official source after it was built
statuses.source-unavailable: due for a check, but the official source is not answering the corpus's pipeline

methods.act-checks: the corpus checks each act against its official source and publishes the result per act (the corpus's data/freshness.json); `last_verified` is the day of its latest check
methods.source-retrieval: the corpus's build read the official source on that day (its REPRODUCE.md); later changes at the source are not known until the next build
methods.stated: the day the corpus states it was last checked (corpus.json `checked_on`)

per_act.note: these corpora publish a freshness row for every act; for a provision in one, `python tools/freshness.py <provision path>` reads its act's row when the corpus is checked out
